title: Styler end rot disease in guava

Header: Styler end rot disease in guava
Phomopsis psidii Sinhala - Phalaagraya kunuweema; Tamil – Koiya mukil adi alukal noi

Prevention: Follow soil test based fertilizer application
Cover fruits with paper bags 3-4 weeks after fruit setting
Prune excess and damaged branches to facilitate aeration and sunlight
Monitoring: Observe discoloration of the region lying just below and adjoining the persistent calyx as a first visible symptom
Observe shrinking of fruits and concentric wrinkles on fruits during later infection
Observe discoloration of internal tissue in severe infected fruits
Restrictions: Apply a fungicide once only at the initial stage of the fruit / before bagging fruits
Toxic to predatory mites, fish and earthworms
Rate of dilution 20g/ 10 lit. of water
Toxic to parasitoids and fish and moderately toxic to predatory mites
